body:
Yes it affects the upstream repo. I submitted a PR there and I believe it was accepted. You might want to check there. Here's a diff on the relevant code in denoise_image.py:```diff-                if y1pad > 0:  # bottom-left-                    ret[:, -y1pad:, :x0pad] = np.flip(self.inimg[:, -y1pad:, :x0pad], axis=(1,2))+                if y1pad > 0:  # bottom-left+                    ret[:, self.cs-y1pad:self.cs, :x0pad] = np.flip(self.inimg[:, self.height-y1pad:self.height, :x0pad], axis=(1,2))``````diff-                if y1pad > 0:  # bottom-right-                    ret[:, -y1pad:, -x1pad:] = np.flip(self.inimg[:, -y1pad:, -x1pad:], axis=(1, 2))+                if y1pad > 0:  # bottom-right+                    ret[:, self.cs-y1pad:self.cs, self.cs-x1pad:self.cs] = np.flip(self.inimg[:, self.height-y1pad:self.height, self.width-x1pad:self.width], axis=(1, 2))```The root cause: `-y1pad` as a negative index into `ret` (size `self.cs`) correctly gives a slice of `y1pad` rows. But the same negative index into `self.inimg` (size `self.height`) gives a different slice size when `self.height` differs from `self.cs`, which is always the case for edge tiles. The fix uses explicit absolute coordinates on both sides.
